gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-sc: Wiry and technical, Nippo pushes small letters near capital size, while Noto Sans SC keeps its curves open and low-key. Nippo grabs attention up top; Noto Sans SC works quietly below.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Nippo lays down its letters like a single line of spaghetti. Noto Sans Soyombo then settles into reading, with a generous x-height and curves that stay open, so paragraphs on screen feel easy going.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagri: Nippo bends neon-glass tubing into letters whose small forms stand close to capital size, a glowing, sign-like opener. Noto Sans Syloti Nagri then hushes things down underneath with short ascenders.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Wire-straight strokes meet blown-glass roundness, with Nippo holding one unbroken line from terminal to junction. And where Nippo excels at that stark line, Noto Sans Syriac excels at plain sans text with easy s turns.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-syriac-eastern: Nippo is wire-bent sign lettering of constant thickness. Against that rigid wire, Noto Sans Syriac Eastern sets lowercase well above its small caps and lets every curve end stay open.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Compact ascenders and pulled-back curve ends keep the body plain sans text, a good foil for the round-pen headings of Nippo. Noto Sans Tai Viet carries paragraphs smoothly, its large x-height holding steady line after line.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-takri: Bent-paperclip lines, zero stroke variation: that is Nippo. Noto Sans Takri brings generously open round letters and a high-waisted lowercase, so a paragraph of text moves along comfortably, line by line.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-tc: Noto Sans TC has large open counters in a, e and s, with curves that flare outward. Noto Sans TC is built for quiet reading, while Nippo does the shouting in wire-bent, constant-thickness strokes.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Bent-copper-pipe strokes give Nippo its whole look, and its small letters rise very close to capital height. Noto Sans Thaana then offers wide, open lowercase forms to settle into.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-thai-looped: Bold-looking lowercase comes from Noto Sans Thai Looped, a sans-serif with spacious curve ends. Make Nippo small and its never-swelling line loses some of its bite; make the body large and it starts to overpower the heading.
